items.title: HUGE: Wipro Flat, HCL Soars - Indian IT's AI Earnings Revealed a Winner and a Loser
items.summary:
India's largest IT services companies held earnings calls this quarter with an unprecedented tone shift. For three decades, the model was predictable: land a multi-year contract, build an offshore team, and renew repeatedly. Now TCS CEO Kitiasan put it bluntly: most AI projects last one to two quarters maximum, forcing firms back to the market every cycle to hunt new deals. Meanwhile, HCL Tech reported 13.9% revenue growth, Wipro posted 0.9% flat growth, and Tech Mahindra led with 17.7% growth, signals that not all Indian IT giants are equal in the AI transition.

In this editorial interview, host Sudhi Sachdev from AIM speaks with tech journalist Ajay Rag to explore what broke the 30-year model: outcome-based pricing vs. labor arbitrage, the rise of forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) as a new job title, token costs becoming a core business metric, and whether HCL Tech's $150 million bet on Serum and data center ownership represents the future or a distraction. The gap between supply and demand for FD talent is severe, and candidates need far more than coding skills, client relations, problem-solving, and sector expertise are now table stakes.

items.title: Bringing Agent-Ready Simulation Into Blender
items.summary:
Robotics, factories, and autonomous systems are creating new demand for simulation-ready 3D worlds — opening new opportunities for the artists and developers who build them.

Now part of NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, NVIDIA Omniverse™ libraries bring agent-ready simulation capabilities into existing 3D applications like Blender. With Omniverse skills, AI agents use these libraries to help turn creative workflows into simulation-ready environments, adding the scene checks, sensor behavior, and physics needed for physical AI.

The result: developers and creators stay in the tools they know while moving content from visually complete to simulation-ready — with more control and less manual integration work.

items.title: From LOOPS to GRAPHS: AI Agents Learn Graph-Based Error Corrections
items.summary:
From LOOPS to GRAPHS.

Test-time RAG, prompt injection, skill.md files, Fused Gromov-Wasserstein (FGW) algorithm, training-time graph-theoretical mathematics. Negative knowledge patterns,  highly specific IF-THEN conditional rules.

Language Models as Agents are too brittle if left to figure everything out on the fly.
MemoHarness introduces Dynamic System Configuration.
EMG introduces Algorithmic Error Routing.

Start with MemoHarness RAG-based control layer to dynamically configure the agent's memory and tools, and then you would use EMG's graph-matching inside the agent's procedural memory to ensure it executes the precise sequence of actions without needing costly reflection loops.
